summary: South African-born tech billionaire Elon Musk, from an abusive wealthy childhood under apartheid through Zip2, PayPal, Tesla and SpaceX, accused of mistreating workers and partners, union-busting, unsafe factories and pushing residents out of Boca Chica, Texas.

evidence.note: Musk born June 1971 in South Africa, start of the covered life story
sons describe psychological abuse by Errol Musk during years living with him
schoolyard gang beats teenage Musk badly enough to hospitalise him
leaves South Africa for Canada, likely dodging apartheid-era conscription
stays on Trump advisory council through immigration crackdowns and Muslim ban
founding of Zip2 with Kimball, first consequential business act
X.com online bank venture, merger into PayPal and ouster as CEO
Roadster carbon fibre paint leads to California pollution fines
SpaceX test site pushes retirees out of Boca Chica, closes public beach
Tesla found to violate labor law by retaliating against union organisers
factory injuries relabelled to lower official counts; safety markings cut
2020 coronavirus tweets and factory reopening bring story to release date

notes: Zip2 founding year (1995) is from general knowledge; the transcript drops the year. Apartheid privilege and possible race-science views are discussed for several minutes but were not added as racism-white-supremacy; reviewer may add it. Grandfather Joshua Haldeman gets only a short segment, so covered_span starts at Musk's birth. The host misgenders Ashley Vance in part 1; corrected at the start of part 2.
